payload.text: hv's standing rules for Utilz work (19 and 20 Oct; the kovacs clause as hv's order of 25 Oct, decision 59, places it). Stack everything outstanding into the next release, with no small releases. Estimates in t-shirt sizes, never wall-clock. A landing is a local commit by path, one at a time into a primary holding no one else's hunks, on vc's word once vc has read the bytes and every booked run at the desk is green; the kovacs legs follow together after the desk work, on the bytes as landed, and a red there reopens its issue before the cut; hv keeps every cut, tag and push. Ready to cut means the final head passes a local twin of every CI job (tests.yml's Ubuntu loop, shellcheck 0.9.0 and Rust fmt and clippy on kovacs; the macOS suites, cargo, acceptance and the menuz app build here), then dc's dry run, so no CI job fails on a slip. A finished issue closes as soon as it lands and is checked; a red on CI or the menuz-app dispatch reopens it.
